C9.2.note: Needed assumptions: the elicited ranking equals actual preference (stated); expressive utility decreases with Kemeny distance (stated as main hypothesis); ceteris paribus regarding pivotality and strategy (stated).

C2.2.reason: The input is modelled as weak preference relations plus approval-type ballots, and the A-Borda points are only an ordinal encoding, so CARD and a separate RANK code are not warranted.

C4.1.reason: The paper formally defines voters' expressive utility as a function of the submitted expressed preference, which is a specified link.

C8.1.reason: C8 applies because VOT is MIXED, and the only behavioural concept is a probabilistic turnout function of utility, which fits OTH rather than an empty list.
